I'm working on constructing a graph with 24 vertices that satisfies several constraints: girth at least 7 (no short cycles), 5-colorability, and at least 33 edges. Since high girth typically means sparse graphs, I'm considering whether known constructions like incidence graphs of generalized polygons might work, though I'm noting that the Heawood graph only has 14 vertices so I'd need something larger.

My approach is to build this greedily by adding edges one at a time while checking that the girth constraint stays satisfied. The 5-colorability should follow naturally since girth 7 graphs with bounded degree tend to be easy to color—if the maximum degree stays around 5 or lower, Brooks' theorem essentially guarantees 5-colorability.
